name: Grosser Aletschgletscher

tier.2016: extrapolated back from the 2017 survey at the cell scale of the first segment; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2017: measured: swissALTI3D 2019 edition (survey 2017), placed at 2017-09-21; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2018: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots); stakes: 1 stake-years, model change = 0.89 of the reading (computed)
tier.2019: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots); stakes: 1 stake-years, model change = 0.57 of the reading (computed)
tier.2020: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; checked against ICESat-2: 334 shots, rmse 1.64 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.57 of the reading (computed)
tier.2021: measured: swissSURFACE3D lidar (60 % of the ice cells, computed; the flight days are in the lidar anchor); checked against ICESat-2: 283 shots, rmse 1.71 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 3 stake-years, model change = 0.59 of the reading (computed)
tier.2022: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; checked against ICESat-2: 121 shots, rmse 1.84 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.64 of the reading (computed)
tier.2023: measured: newest swissALTI3D edition (2024 edition, aerial images 2023), placed at 2023-08-10; checked against ICESat-2: 373 shots, rmse 1.38 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.77 of the reading (computed)
tier.2024: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; checked against ICESat-2: 718 shots, rmse 2.40 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.70 of the reading (computed)
tier.2025: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.73 of the reading (computed)
tier.2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch: provisional; checked against ICESat-2: 443 shots, rmse 3.10 m (leave-one-granule-out)

summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2017, 2023), swisstopo lidar (25 tiles of 2021) and the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per elevation band for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: Image strips over the strip in 2017 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2017-07-17 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (40 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-08-07 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (40 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-08-29 SWISSIMAGE (15 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-09-08 SWISSIMAGE (60 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-09-21 SWISSIMAGE (99 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published; the edition is a composite of the strips that cover each cell, and the model puts all of it on one day.
anchors.placed_at: 2017-09-21 (a day a strip was flown; the pair of flown strip days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (2.23 m; leave-one-granule-out 2.23 m); days within 0.05 m of it cannot be separated by the shots and the tie goes to the GLAMOS date of the edition if it is one of them, else to the strip covering most ice; chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 26 tiles read (tiles with ice). 10 tiles hold at least 85 % of their points on a single day (2021-09-24 on 9, 2021-08-21 on 1); 15 tiles were flown on several days within 60 days and take the point-weighted mean day (uncertain by up to about a month); 1 tiles flown on days further apart (or not read) are not used. The lidar sits on 60 % of the ice cells (computed).

built from aerial images 2023: strips over the ice 2023-08-10 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (32 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-08-10 DISASTER MAPPING (7 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-09-05 SWISSIMAGE (30 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-09-06 SWISSIMAGE (100 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2023-08-10 (a day a strip was flown; the pair of flown strip days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (2.23 m; leave-one-granule-out 2.23 m); days within 0.05 m of it cannot be separated by the shots and the tie goes to the GLAMOS date of the edition if it is one of them, else to the strip covering most ice; chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of the ice by elevation band: from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt uniform from 1 May: ASSUMPTION) to 30 September. The band balance of each year is the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletschgletscher itself (release 2025, 100 m elevation bins from 1634 m, which cover the whole tongue; non-commercial). It only sets HOW the change between two surveys is spread over the years and elevations; the SIZE comes from the surveys. 2026 is not in GLAMOS release 2025: its glacier-wide balance is READ FROM THE GLAMOS FIGURE (winter +751.6 mm w.e., annual -3038.4 mm w.e., about +-100 mm w.e.) and spread to the 100 m bands with the figure's melt timing. Other band balances were tried on the same ICESat-2 shots (rmse over all shots, computed): the borrowed line 2.06 m (covers only 73 % of the ice cells: not eligible); Corbassiere 2.08 m (covers only 74 % of the ice cells: not eligible); Rhone 2.09 m; Findel 2.20 m (covers only 29 % of the ice cells: not eligible); Grosser Aletsch (own bands) 2.23 m; the glacier's own measured balance is used wherever one exists. Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the cell scale of the last segment is kept, applied to the measured 2023 surface with its own detail: the change comes from the difference of the anchor surfaces smoothed over about 100 m (median of 5 cells of 20 m, then a light Gaussian), because the raw cell by cell difference carries the noise and crevasse detail of surveys of different vintage and made 2024 to 2026 rough. The ground outside the 2023 ice outline is held at its 2023 height and no fade of the lowering towards the outline is applied (the 80 m fade is Gorner only, owner 2026-11-01), so a step grows along the outline: median lowering of the ice cells next to it 2.6 m in 2024, 4.8 m in 2025, 7.8 m in 2026 (computed). Every cell stays between its two anchors, or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band (in m of ice) of the nearest anchor. The tip lake of 2024, 2025 and 2026 is flat at the level set earlier (an assumption: the real level is not known), with a raised rim.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007, 2272 shots on 2023 ice, July to October, slope under 20 degrees, quality 0, h_li_sigma under 1 m, not more than 10 m above the higher of the two surveys and inside the physical envelope (not below 2 x (A2 - A1) - 10 m from the A1 surface), in 9 granules: rmse 2.23 m over all years, bias 0.58 m, leave-one-granule-out (for each granule the A1 and A2 days are chosen on the other granules and the held-out granule is scored); with the days used (2017-09-21 and 2023-08-10) rmse 2.23 m (error = model minus shot). Per year (leave-one-granule-out): 2020 1.64 m (334 shots); 2021 1.71 m (283 shots); 2022 1.84 m (121 shots); 2023 1.38 m (373 shots); 2024 2.40 m (718 shots); 2026 3.10 m (443 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 10163 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.18 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September). ICESat-2 scores the surface in the years with shots, not each year step. ASTER AST14DEM scenes (NASA LP DAAC, July to October 2016 to 2026) were checked against the model: scene used if at least 300 rock and 200 ice cells and a rock NMAD of at most 15 m, offset from stable rock; 10 of 82 scenes passed (years 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022). ASTER is rough, so only differences of a few metres per year mean something. GLAMOS stake readings (25 stake-years, annual files, type 1, on modelled ice inside the 2023 outline) are a check of the year-to-year split: the modelled surface change is 0.68 of the stake reading on average (RMSE 1.05 m), as expected because stakes move with the ice.
validation.extended_area: Cells farther than 1 km from every ICESat-2 shot used for the check (8,148 of 49,849 modelled ice cells, computed) have no check; above 2,000 m swisstopo derives heights from stereo images (accuracy "1 to 3 m", swisstopo page).

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: Airborne DEMs of 2009, 2011 and 2017 (RAGMAC set; readmes say internal use only). The 2011 DEM is a composite with 2009 flights and DHM25 and sits above the ASTER thinning curve on the ice. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (use, processing and commercial use allowed, source "Federal Office of Topography swisstopo"; terms page read 2026-10-30). GLAMOS balances: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2: used for checking only.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch: provisional; checked against ICESat-2: 443 shots, rmse 3.10 m (leave-one-granule-out)

page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 21.1 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2017 survey, about 23.1 km² (computed). The 2,272 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). The ICESat-2 check covers the cells within 1 km of a shot; the rest, 16 % of the modelled ice cells (8,148 of 49,849, computed), follows the same rules but has no check. Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface (2016 is itself extrapolated back from the 2017 survey).
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the survey days of both anchors, so not an independent check; the rmse is leave-one-granule-out (the days are chosen on the other granules).
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 6.6 to 14.3 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.
page.stakeNote: Over all 25 stake-years the modelled surface change is 0.68 of the stake reading (RMSE 1.05 m). Stakes read ablation of moving ice, so the model is expected to show a fraction. By year the ratio is 2018 0.89, 2019 0.57, 2020 0.57, 2021 0.59, 2022 0.64, 2023 0.77, 2024 0.70, 2025 0.73 (computed). Check only, not in the fit.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). The two swisstopo surveys carry 1.38 m (rmse of the 373 shots of 2023; swisstopo quotes 0.5 m below 2000 m and 1 to 3 m above, as quoted by Bannwart et al., so the true value may be larger on a tongue this high), the lidar of 2021 1.43 m (rmse of 62 shots within 45 days of the lidar day). Between the surveys and beyond them the error grows with the size of the change (factors 0.12 and 0.20), calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots, so it is not independent. Where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2025) rest on the formula alone. 2026 has no value on the chart: it is an estimate (its balance is estimated from a figure for Aletsch), and its map in the viewer adds 25 % of its increment (median 3.6 m).
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also chose the survey days of both anchors and calibrated σ, so it is not independent (rmse is leave-one-granule-out). ASTER scenes are checks only (10 of 82 scenes usable; usable years: 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022). GLAMOS stakes (25 stake-years on modelled ice) are checks only. Click a year for the numbers.
notes.sharing: Solid: the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per elevation band sets how the loss between two surveys falls into each year. Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance); the years before the first survey are extrapolated back. Not used: measured years.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and GLAMOS stakes (orange: stake, purple: automatic camera) and hover a record for its values. About 17 MB, loaded when you press the button.

bed.lead: Three checks on Grosser Aletsch (all computed here, not source figures). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 2,603 radar cells, how far apart are the two beds?

Median about 0 m in every survey year: −0.2 m (2011, 1,679 cells), −0.6 m (2009, 765), +1.1 m (1958 seismic, 159). Spread (standard deviation) 7 to 12 m; 81 % of cells within 10 m, 99 % within 30 m.

Reading: close, but not a validation. The model was made from these same surveys, and at the survey lines its bed is the measured bed (Grab et al. 2021, where the survey surface agreed with a DEM).

2 · 2009 against 2011

Where both years surveyed the same spot, how well do they repeat?

At 558 spots (25 m cells) the beds implied by the two surveys differ with a standard deviation of 17.9 m, and only 52 % agree within 10 m. The thickness change 2009 to 2011 has a median of −3.0 m (482 cells of 50 m) against a spread of 20.5 m.

Reading: single radar cells are noisy at the scale of tens of metres; only medians mean anything.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

142 points (81 from 2009, 61 from 2011), ice about 79 m thick:

20092011
Radar bed − ground now+6.6 m (+4.3 to +8.5)+8.7 m (−1.0 to +19.1)
Model bed − ground now+0.5 m (−1.9 to +3.1)+2.7 m (−0.9 to +5.1)

Median, in brackets the middle half. 81 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now, a median 12 % of the thickness.

bed.key: Each dot is one radar point of 2009 or 2011 on the lower tongue, in ground that is ice free in the newest swissALTI3D. Light blue: ice in the SGI2023 outline; dashed: the SGI2016 outline, the ice the model was made for. The points lie in the strip between the two outlines, kept 30 m clear of both. They come from only 5 places along the margin, where flight lines cross it, so the 142 points are not 142 independent samples.
bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins the model bed sits within a few metres of the exposed ground. The radar bed lies about 7 m (a tenth of the thickness) above it.
  • So at the margins the radar thickness reads too small, or the survey's surface height too high, or both. The data cannot separate the two. The helicopter surveys take the surface from GPS minus the radar-measured air layer and check it against a DEM "when an up-to-date" one exists (Rutishauser et al. 2016); which DEM, is not stated.
  • On the section chart: the dashed model bed is the line to read, the radar dots are measurements that carry this offset.

What it does not show

  • Few places: the 142 points come from 5 crossings of the margin by flight lines (3, 32, 66, 37 and 4 points), so the medians rest on a handful of locations.
  • Not the deep tongue: these are margin points, about 80 m of ice; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • Not a model error band: the model's own uncertainty maps are not in the GLAMOS release, and swissBEDROCK's uncertainty band under glaciers is about 0 (not usable). The model is also called "a maximum estimate" of the bed by its release notes.
  • Not screened: lakes and debris on the exposed ground, and positions at the margin (a few metres of horizontal error).

How the ice-free points were chosen

  • On the tongue, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline (acquired 2023, all glaciers) and at least 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there. Outside SGI2016 the model bed equals the ground by construction and proves nothing.
  • Newest swissALTI3D edition, ground slope at the point at most 20°. With up to 30°: 195 points, the same result (radar +6.4 m, model +0.8 m). With a 50 m margin only 12 points remain (radar +7.8 m, model −2.1 m); with 100 m none.
